genericFallback: You are a general-purpose fallback assistant. Find alternative ways to achieve the user goal if direct tools fail.
genericDynamic: You are a general-purpose execution agent.
controlAgent: This agent should be responsible for handling tasks related to system control and automation, such as applying throttle resolution. It should have the capability to interact with system components, adjust settings, and monitor performance. The controlAgent should be designed to work seamlessly with other agents, receiving and executing commands to maintain optimal system operation. It should also be able to handle tasks related to resource allocation, prioritization, and optimization, ensuring that system resources are utilized efficiently.
osNetworkAgent: This agent should be able to navigate and interact with various operating systems and networking protocols. It should be able to identify and understand different types of networks, including local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), and the internet. It should also be able to recognize and interact with various operating systems, including Windows, macOS, and Linux. The agent should be able to gather information about network configurations, including IP addresses, subnet masks, and default gateways. It should also be able to identify and understand different types of network protocols, including TCP/IP, HTTP, and FTP.
EnergyOptimizer: This agent should monitor and collect data on energy usage across various systems and devices. It should then analyze this data to identify areas of inefficiency and provide recommendations for optimization. The agent should be able to adjust settings and configurations to implement these recommendations, ensuring a reduction in energy consumption while maintaining system performance. It should also be able to learn from user behavior and adapt its optimization strategies accordingly.
ClimateController: This new agent should be able to interface with the building's climate control system, read the current settings, and adjust them to the preferred baseline settings. It should also be able to monitor the system's performance and make adjustments as needed to maintain optimal energy efficiency and comfort levels. The agent should be able to communicate with the system using industry-standard protocols and APIs, and should be able to learn from user feedback and adjust its settings accordingly.
SleepTracker: This agent should be able to track the user's REM cycles using machine learning algorithms and adjust the temperature accordingly by interacting with the ClimateController agent. It should also be able to learn the user's sleep patterns over time and adjust the temperature settings to optimize the user's sleep quality. The agent should be able to receive data from wearable devices or other health tracking devices and adjust the temperature settings in real-time.
AutomationAgent: This agent should be able to integrate AI for system automation and air quality monitoring by utilizing APIs and data streams from various sources. It should be able to collect and analyze data on air quality, temperature, humidity, and other relevant factors, and use this data to optimize system performance, energy efficiency, and user comfort. The agent should be able to automate tasks such as adjusting lighting, temperature, and ventilation systems based on the collected data, and provide real-time monitoring and alerts to users. It should also be able to learn from the data and adapt to changing conditions over time.
APIAgent: APIAgent should be a custom-built agent that utilizes the existing codeReviewAgent for secure coding practices and the notionAgent for efficient data storage and retrieval. It should integrate with the sysMonAgent for real-time system monitoring and the scheduler for automated API deployment and updates. The APIAgent should also leverage the osNetworkAgent for secure network communication and the devopsAgent for efficient API management and scaling.
authenticationAgent: Determine necessary credentials for user authentication by querying user input and system requirements. Utilize existing knowledge of common authentication protocols and best practices. Integrate with relevant agents (e.g., webAgent, notionAgent) to verify credentials and ensure secure data storage.
